Hi Samir — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the same priorities before the on-site/network test next week. I attached a draft SLO proposal (Redwood SLO proposal) and a short runbook link for the test.

High-level goals we heard today:
- End-to-end 95th percentile response time target (app visible): <= 120 ms
- Inference-only P95 target: <= 60 ms for standard text-gen workloads
- Streaming/chunk latency (user-facing token delivery): <= 200 ms chunk interval
- Sustained throughput target for pilot: ~200 requests/sec with bursts to 400 req/sec
- Concurrent sessions: target concurrency 50 active sessions during peak

Network path & egress considerations we need to qualify:
- Preferred connectivity: Direct peering (private VPC peering) vs IPsec VPN — you mentioned peering is preferred if available in your region.
- Egress hop budget: please confirm expected intra-VPC latency and egress NAT layer timing (we estimate +8–15 ms if egress goes through your NAT/egress appliances)
- MTU and packet-loss budget for streaming (we recommend enabling path MTU discovery and keeping average packet loss <0.1% during tests)

Action items (owner — due):
1) Arkwell network team to provide traceroutes and any ipsec/peering configs we can test against — Samir / Priya (EOD 2027-05-17)
2) Redwood infra to prepare a streaming-specific profile and KV-cache-enabled model variant for the test — Vivek (2027-05-18)
3) Agree on a perf test window and runbook steps, run a short preflight with synthetic traffic — Lauren/Rishi coordinate (schedule by 2027-05-18)

Attachments:
- redwood-slo-proposal.pdf (attached) — initial SLOs and test checklist
- Runbook link: https://drive.google.com/arkwell/onprem/runbook

If anything above is incorrect or missing, please flag. If the timeline works, let's lock an on-call test for Thursday 2027-05-20 (30–60 minute window).

Thanks,

Corrections/notes:
- Our app-level budget is tighter at times; 120 ms end-to-end is the desirable maximum, but real-world targets for interactive features should aim for 80–100 ms. We'll prioritize the 100 ms budget for the pilot if you can demonstrate consistent inference P95 <= 60 ms.
- We strongly prefer private peering (VPC peering + route injection) for the pilot. We can provision a BGP peering in us-east-1 and give you a private route to the inference subnet. If BGP peering isn't feasible, we'll fall back to an IPsec tunnel.

Looking forward to the test on 5/20 — I'll confirm a time once Priya and I sync.

Thanks Samir / Lauren. Quick technical notes after reviewing the trace and the SLO ask — copying an internal checklist we'll use for the preflight.

Checklist & recommendations:
- Traceroute review: I saw two middle hops that add ~7-10ms each on some samples. We need the full set of traces from your primary peering router and any transit providers to rule out transient buffering. (Samir, Priya: can you export the last 24h traces from edge routers?)
- Peering: preferred. If you can provision a BGP session, we will test with route-based peering + MTU 1500. If peering is delayed, the IPsec tunnel must be tuned for MTU and reordering (we recommend fragmentation offload disabled on the tunnel endpoints).
- Streaming behavior: enable smaller model chunk sizes + KV cache warmup on the start of a session. For safety margin set chunk delivery <= 250 ms during the first pass; if we see stable latencies we'll reduce to 200 ms.
- Concurrency & batching: we will run a load matrix (50, 100, 200 concurrent sessions) with both steady and burst patterns. Please note that request coalescing on the Redwood side can change per-token latency at high concurrency — we'll share a heatmap after the first run.
- Egress NAT: confirm your egress appliance capacity (pps) and whether SNAT is applied per-subnet or per-VPC. SNAT-induced connection tracking can add jitter under load.

Action items (technical):
- Arkwell: export router traces and confirm whether peering BGP is possible (Samir/Priya) — due 2027-05-17 EOD
- Redwood infra (me): prepare streaming profile and test harness + provide sample iperf commands and VPN config tuning notes — due 2027-05-18
- Redwood ops (Rishi): coordinate the scheduled test window and provide HubSpot test record link — due 2027-05-18

I'll attach a small sample VPN tuning snippet we use in tests (vpn-config-sample.txt). We should also decide whether to enable prefix-level health checks to failover to a fallback region during the run.
